about: Persona quiz: 5 questions -> run_agent(style_text=..., budget_usd=...). Scored by agent/quiz.py. Styles are data/sie.py STYLES. Images are hotlinked from their sources (not ours, not committed); each option names the page it came from and the search that found it, collected 2026-11-20.
image_rights: Images belong to their owners. Hotlinked for the demo with source credit. Several Pinterest pins look AI-generated. Replace with our own or IKEA catalog photos before any public use beyond the demo.

questions.prompt: It's Friday night. Which room do you want to walk into?
questions.psychology: Gut reaction first. People rarely know style names but react to a room quickly and consistently. Four options keep the choice fast (Hick's law).
references: Zajonc, R. B. (1980). Feeling and thinking: Preferences need no inferences. American Psychologist, 35(2), 151-175.
Hick, W. E. (1952). On the rate of gain of information. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 4(1), 11-26.

questions.prompt: Which one would you want to touch every day?
questions.psychology: Materials, not rooms. Touch preference is a stable personal trait and separates styles that look alike from across a room (oak vs walnut, linen vs leather). These words also go into style_text, which the Superlinked reranker matches against IKEA's colour and material text.
references: Peck, J., & Childers, T. L. (2003). Individual differences in haptic information processing: The "need for touch" scale. Journal of Consumer Research, 30(3), 430-442.

questions.prompt: Which room would you NOT want to live in?
questions.psychology: People are surer about what they dislike than what they like, and a bad pick costs them more than a good one pleases them. One rejection removes a whole style. It only lowers that style's score; it is never written into style_text, because a reranker can match the word in 'not industrial' and rank industrial higher.
references: Baumeister, R. F., Bratslavsky, E., Finkenauer, C., & Vohs, K. D. (2001). Bad is stronger than good. Review of General Psychology, 5(4), 323-370.
Kahneman, D., & Tversky, A. (1979). Prospect theory: An analysis of decision under risk. Econometrica, 47(2), 263-291.

questions.psychology: Ask what the room is for, not what the person likes. Use beats taste when the two disagree (white linen with a dog). The answer adds words to style_text that the reranker reads; it changes no style score.
references: Christensen, C. M., Hall, T., Dillon, K., & Duncan, D. S. (2016). Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice. Harper Business.

questions.prompt: What's the most you'd spend on any one piece, like the sofa?
questions.psychology: Fixed bands with no default selected, so we don't plant an anchor number. Per piece because the agent applies budget_usd to each pick. 'Not sure' is allowed instead of forcing a guess.
references: Tversky, A., & Kahneman, D. (1974). Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases. Science, 185(4157), 1124-1131.
